title.en: At the kiosk, the bakery and the café: asking for what you want

blocks.tr:
Bu bölümde **büfeden ve fırından alışveriş yapmayı** ve **kahve ısmarlamayı** öğreneceksin; fiyatı, avro ile senti, kilo ile gramı da.

Anahtar nokta: istediğin şey fiilin **nesnesi** olunca artikel değişir: *ο καφές* ama **θέλω τον καφέ**; *η τυρόπιτα* ama **θέλω την τυρόπιτα**. Eril isim de sondaki *-ς*'yi atar.
blocks.en:
In this chapter you learn to **buy at a kiosk and a bakery** and to **order coffee**, with prices, euros and cents, kilos and grams.

The key point: when the thing you want is the **object** of the verb, the article changes: *ο καφές* but **θέλω τον καφέ**; *η τυρόπιτα* but **θέλω την τυρόπιτα**. A masculine noun also drops its final *-ς*.

blocks.tr: Dinle, sonra oku. Kalıplar: [[Κάτι άλλο;]] (başka bir şey?), [[Τι θα θέλατε;]] (ne arzu edersiniz?), [[Πάμε!]] (hadi gidelim!) ve *Θα ήθελα…* (… isterdim). *Πάω* fiilinin biçimleri aşağıda.
blocks.en: Listen, then read. Set phrases: [[Κάτι άλλο;]] (anything else?), [[Τι θα θέλατε;]] (what would you like?), [[Πάμε!]] (let's go!) and *Θα ήθελα…* (I'd like). The forms of *πάω* follow below.

setting.tr: Ayşe sabah erkenden büfeye uğruyor. Kostas büfeci.
setting.en: Early in the morning Ayşe stops at the kiosk. Kostas runs it.

lines.el: Καλημέρα σας. Θα ήθελα ένα νερό και μια εφημερίδα, παρακαλώ.
lines.tr: Günaydın. Bir su ve bir gazete alayım, lütfen.
lines.en: Good morning. I'd like a water and a newspaper, please.
No, thank you. How much is it?

setting.tr: Sonra fırın. Ayşe tezgâhtaki ürünleri parmağıyla gösteriyor.
setting.en: Then the bakery. Ayşe points at what she wants.

lines.el: Καλημέρα. Θέλω αυτή την τυρόπιτα και ένα κουλούρι.
lines.tr: Günaydın. Şu peynirli böreği ve bir simit istiyorum.
lines.en: Good morning. I want this cheese pie and a bread ring.
Yes. How much is the bread?
I'd like five hundred grams, please.

lines.el: Ορίστε. Τρία ευρώ και πενήντα λεπτά.
lines.en: Here you are. Three euros fifty.

setting.tr: Ayşe fırından çıkıyor ve arkadaşı Nikos'a rastlıyor. Birlikte kafeye gidiyorlar; garson Giorgos.
setting.en: Ayşe leaves the bakery and meets her friend Nikos. They go to a café together; Giorgos is the waiter.

lines.en: Good morning, Ayşe! Where are you going?

lines.el: Καλημέρα, Νίκο! Πήγα στο περίπτερο και στον φούρνο. Πάω για καφέ. Θέλεις κι εσύ;
lines.tr: Günaydın Nikos! Büfeye ve fırına gittim. Kahveye gidiyorum. Sen de ister misin?
lines.en: Good morning, Nikos! I went to the kiosk and the bakery. I'm going for a coffee. Do you want one too?
Good morning. What would you like?

lines.tr: Sade mi, orta mı, şekerli mi?

lines.el: Εγώ θα ήθελα έναν φραπέ και ένα νερό.
lines.tr: Ben bir frappe ve bir su alayım.
lines.en: I'd like a frappé and a water.
Thank you. How much is it?

lines.el: Αϊσέ, αύριο θα πας στον φούρνο; Θέλω κι εγώ ένα κουλούρι.
lines.tr: Ayşe, yarın fırına gidecek misin? Ben de bir simit istiyorum.
lines.en: Ayşe, will you go to the bakery tomorrow? I want a bread ring too.

lines.el: Ναι, θα πάω. Ένα κουλούρι για τον Νίκο!
lines.en: Yes, I will. A bread ring for Nikos!

title.tr: İki artikel: ο, η, το ve ένας, μια, ένα
title.en: Two articles: ο, η, το and ένας, μια, ένα

blocks.tr: **Belirli artikel** *ο, η, το*'yu ("the") tanıyorsun. Bir de **belirsiz artikel** var: **ένας, μια, ένα** ("bir"), aynı zamanda "bir" sayısı. Bir şeyi isterken belirsiz artikel kullanırsın: **ένα νερό**.
blocks.en: You know the **definite article** *ο, η, το* ("the"). There is also an **indefinite article**: **ένας, μια, ένα** ("a, an"), which is also the number "one". You use it to ask for something: **ένα νερό**.

note.tr: *Μια* yazıda *μία* diye de yazılır; ikisi de doğru.
note.en: *Μια* is also written *μία*; both are correct.

items.el: Μια τυρόπιτα και ένα κουλούρι, παρακαλώ.
items.tr: Bir peynirli börek ve bir simit lütfen.
items.en: A cheese pie and a bread ring, please.

title.tr: İstediğin şey nesnedir: τον, την, έναν
title.en: What you want is the object: τον, την, έναν

blocks.tr: İstediğin, okuduğun ya da beklediğin şey fiilin **nesnesidir** (*θέλω, διαβάζω, περιμένω*). Nesne **αιτιατική** hâlindedir; bunu *στον, στην, στο*'dan tanıyorsun. Özne yalın hâlde (*ονομαστική*) kalır. [[θέλει]]: (o) istiyor.
blocks.en: The thing you want, read or wait for is the **object** of the verb (*θέλω, διαβάζω, περιμένω*). It takes the **accusative** (*αιτιατική*), which you know from *στον, στην, στο*. The subject stays in the nominative (*ονομαστική*). [[θέλει]]: he/she wants.

note.tr: Eril en çok değişir: *ο → τον, ένας → έναν*, isim de sondaki *-ς*'yi atar (*καφές → καφέ*). Dişilde yalnızca artikel değişir: *η → την* (ya da *τη*, -ν kuralı); *μια* ve isim aynı kalır. Nötr hiç değişmez.
note.en: The masculine changes most: *ο → τον, ένας → έναν*, and the noun drops its final *-ς* (*καφές → καφέ*). In the feminine only the article changes: *η → την* (or *τη*, by the -ν rule); *μια* and the noun stay the same. The neuter does not change at all.

blocks.tr: **-ν kuralı:** *τον* ve *έναν* her zaman -ν'li yazılır (*ένα καφέ* da duyarsın; sen *έναν* yaz). *Την* ise ünlüden ve κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, μπ, ντ, γκ, τσ, τζ'dan önce -ν'yi korur: *την εφημερίδα, την τυρόπιτα*. Diğer ünsüzlerden önce düşer: *τη σοκολάτα*.
blocks.en: **The -ν rule:** *τον* and *έναν* always keep the -ν (you also hear *ένα καφέ*; write *έναν*). *Την* keeps it before a vowel and before κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, μπ, ντ, γκ, τσ, τζ: *την εφημερίδα, την τυρόπιτα*. Before other consonants it drops: *τη σοκολάτα*.

items.en: The customer wants a cheese pie.

note.tr: *Ο πελάτης* özne: yalın hâl. *Μια τυρόπιτα* nesne.
note.en: *Ο πελάτης* is the subject: nominative. *Μια τυρόπιτα* is the object.

items.el: Η Αϊσέ θέλει τη σοκολάτα, όχι την τυρόπιτα.
items.tr: Ayşe çikolatayı istiyor, peynirli böreği değil.
items.en: Ayşe wants the chocolate, not the cheese pie.

note.tr: σ listede yok, bu yüzden *τη*; τ listede, bu yüzden *την*.
note.en: σ is not on the list, so *τη*; τ is, so *την*.

title.tr: "Bu": αυτός ο, αυτή η, αυτό το
title.en: "This": αυτός ο, αυτή η, αυτό το

blocks.tr: Bir şeyi gösterirken **αυτός, αυτή, αυτό** ("bu, şu") dersin. İkinci dersten *αυτός* ve *αυτή* kelimelerini "o" olarak biliyorsun; isimle birlikte "bu" anlamına gelir. Yunancada **artikel yine de kalır**: *αυτός **ο** καφές*. Eril nesnede ikisi de değişir: *αυτόν τον καφέ*.
blocks.en: To point at something, say **αυτός, αυτή, αυτό** ("this"). You know *αυτός* and *αυτή* as "he" and "she" from Lesson 2; with a noun they mean "this". Greek **keeps the article** too: *αυτός **ο** καφές*. For a masculine object both words change: *αυτόν τον καφέ*.

note.tr: Kurala göre *αυτήν την* daha doğrudur (*την* τ ile başlıyor), ama *αυτή την* çok daha sık. Çoğul biçimler sonra.
note.en: By the -ν rule *αυτήν την* is stricter (*την* starts with τ), but *αυτή την* is far more common. Plurals come later.

items.en: How much is this bread ring?

title.tr: Sipariş ve ödeme: kalıplar, avro, kilo
title.en: Ordering and paying: phrases, euros, kilos

blocks.tr: **Θέλω** ("istiyorum") doğrudandır; **Θα ήθελα** daha kibardır ve her yerde duyulur. İkisini de kalıp olarak öğren.
blocks.en: **Θέλω** ("I want") is direct; **Θα ήθελα** is more polite, and you hear it everywhere. Learn both as set phrases.

rows.tr: Ne kadar? (bir şey ya da toplam)
rows.en: How much is it? (one thing, or the total)
Here you are; yes? (the seller asking)

blocks.tr:
**Para.** *Ευρώ* hiç değişmez: *ένα ευρώ, δύο ευρώ*. Sent **λεπτό**'dur: *πενήντα λεπτά*. Fiyatta virgül kullanılır: 2,50 €.

**Ağırlık.** *Ένα κιλό* = *χίλια γραμμάρια*; yarım kilo *μισό κιλό* ya da *πεντακόσια γραμμάρια* (*γραμμάρια* çoğul biçimdir).
blocks.en:
**Money.** *Ευρώ* never changes: *ένα ευρώ, δύο ευρώ*. A cent is a **λεπτό**: *πενήντα λεπτά*. Prices use a comma: 2,50 €.

**Weight.** *Ένα κιλό* = *χίλια γραμμάρια*; half a kilo is *μισό κιλό* or *πεντακόσια γραμμάρια* (*γραμμάρια* is the plural).

note.tr: Konuşurken kısa: *δύο πενήντα* ya da *δυόμισι* (iki buçuk).
note.en: Spoken, often short: *δύο πενήντα*, or *δυόμισι* (two and a half).

blocks.tr: Kahvenin türü ve şekeri tek kelimeyle söylenir. Bu kelimeler eril *ο καφές* ile gider, bu yüzden sipariş verirken (*έναν …*) nesne biçimini alır: sondaki *-ος* → *-ο*, *-ές* → *-έ*. Sıfatları sekizinci derste öğreneceksin; şimdilik bu kelimeleri hazır kalıp olarak al.
blocks.en: The type of coffee and its sugar are each one word. They go with masculine *ο καφές*, so when you order (*έναν …*) they take the object form: *-ος* → *-ο*, *-ές* → *-έ*. Adjectives come in Lesson 8; take these words as ready-made for now.

rows.en: Greek coffee (brewed in a small pot, like Turkish coffee)

note.tr: Çok kişi *ένα φραπέ* de der: o zaman *φραπέ* nötrdür ve hiç değişmez. İkisi de anlaşılır; bu kitap *ο φραπές, έναν φραπέ* kullanıyor.
note.en: Many people also say *ένα φραπέ*: then *φραπέ* is neuter and never changes. Both are understood; this book uses *ο φραπές, έναν φραπέ*.

items.tr: Orta şekerli bir Yunan kahvesi lütfen.

items.en: I'd like a sweet Greek coffee.

blocks.tr: **Πάω** (gitmek) fiilinin geçmişini ve geleceğini **hazır biçimler** olarak öğren, şimdilik yalnızca *ben* ve *sen* için. Geçmişte kök değişir: *πήγα*. Gelecek **θα** + biçimdir. Gidilen yer *σε* + nesne hâli: *πάω στο περίπτερο*. *Χθες* dün, *αύριο* yarın demektir.
blocks.en: Learn the past and future of **πάω** (to go) as **ready-made forms**, for *I* and *you* only. The past has a new stem, *πήγα*; the future is **θα** + the form. Where you go is *σε* + the accusative: *πάω στο περίπτερο*. *Χθες* is yesterday, *αύριο* tomorrow.

items.en: Yesterday I went to the bakery.
Tomorrow I'll go to the kiosk.

blocks.tr: Bu dersin kelimeleri: büfe ve fırın ürünleri, para ve ağırlık, kahve türleri, *πάω*. *Ο φούρνος* da Türkçedeki *fırın* gibi hem yemek pişirilen fırın hem ekmek fırını demektir.
blocks.en: The words of this lesson: kiosk and bakery things, money and weight, coffee types, and *πάω*. *Ο φούρνος* means both "oven" and "bakery".

blocks.tr: **Türkçeden bir köprü.** Türkçede belirli nesne ek alır: *kahveyi istiyorum* = *θέλω τον καφέ*. *Bir kahve istiyorum*'da ise ek yok. Yunancada ikisi de nesne biçimini alır: *τον καφέ* ve *έναν καφέ*.
blocks.en: **A bridge.** English shows the object form only on pronouns: *he* → *him*. Greek shows it on the article and on a masculine noun, even after *a*: *έναν καφέ*.

blocks.tr: **Είμαι'den sonra nesne biçimi gelmez.** *Είμαι* ile söylenen şey yalın hâlde kalır: *Ο Γιώργος είναι ο σερβιτόρος*; *Ο Γιώργος είναι **τον** σερβιτόρο* yanlış.
blocks.en: **No accusative after είμαι.** With *είμαι* the thing named stays in the nominative: *Ο Γιώργος είναι ο σερβιτόρος*, not *τον σερβιτόρο*.

blocks.tr: Şimdi sen dene: nesne biçimi, "bu", gitmek.
blocks.en: Now you try: the object form, "this", and going.
